summary.note: model-assisted search; author confirmation pending for every row

coverage_notes.AE: AE (CBUAE, Digital Dirham). Searched: centralbank.ae (behind a Cloudflare challenge; plain HTTP requests are blocked, headless Chromium passes after ~25 s per fresh session) - press release pages and PDFs under centralbank.ae/media, CBUAE policy papers and working papers pages (Digital Dirham primer, Working Paper 1/2025), FinTech & Digital Transformation page, annual reports (2023, 2024 press release, 2025), mBridge page; CBUAE Rulebook (rulebook.centralbank.ae, Federal Decree-Law 54/2023 and the consolidated FDL 14/2018); UAE Legislation portal (uaelegislation.gov.ae, FDL 6/2025 and its news item); Government of Dubai Media Office (MoF/Dubai Finance release); web search for CBUAE releases 2023-2026. Period covered: 2019 (Project Aber) to Oct 2026. The CBUAE news listing and site search are JavaScript-rendered and could not be listed in full, so press releases were found through web search plus direct PDF retrieval; there may be a few minor releases I did not see (e.g. a Dec 2025 CBUAE announcement that the first phase will be free for individuals and SMEs is reported in the press, but I found no official text). Dated items: FDL 54/2023 is dated by its 1 Nov 2023 effective date. The 2025 annual report was read only through a text extract (direct download returned 404). Judgement: MAJOR GAPS. The registry has only 3 rows (the 2023 strategy press release, the July 2025 primer, the 2025 symbol press release). It lacks both laws that give the digital dirham legal-tender status, the July 2025 staff working paper with explicit privacy/pseudonymity/holding-limit content, the July 2025 release that announces near-term launch with offline and smart-contract features, the 2023 annual report that records first issuance and the retail pilot, and the Nov 2025 pilot-phase launch. Candidates: 9, 1 of them wholesale-only (mBridge MVP).
coverage_notes.AU: AU (RBA; eAUD pilot; Project Acacia; Treasury). Searched: rba.gov.au tokenised-money section (current-initiatives, publications, Retail CBDC FAQs, speeches list; the old /central-bank-digital-currency/ URLs now redirect to /tokenised-money/), RBA media releases 2021-2026 (mr-21-12, mr-22-23, mr-22-31, mr-23-06, mr-23-21, mr-24-17, mr-26-24), RBA speeches (Richards 2020, Lowe 2021, Jones 2024), RBA Bulletin and Research Discussion Papers (Bulletin Sep 2020, RDP 2024-02), the Treasury publication pages (p2023-404960 Strategic Plan, p2024-581588 joint paper), plus web search for RBA/Treasury CBDC items. Covered 2020 to Oct 2026. The site was reachable with plain HTTP. The RBA speeches page is filtered by JavaScript and shows all speeches, so CBDC speeches were found through search. There may be further panel or testimony remarks with brief CBDC statements that I did not list. Judgement: MAJOR GAPS before this check. The registry lacks the central September 2024 RBA-Treasury joint paper, which records the decision to prioritise wholesale over retail and has a privacy section, together with its media release and the Jones speech. It also lacks the earlier posture statements (Richards 2020, Lowe 2021), the staff privacy research (RDP 2024-02, Bulletin 2020), the Treasury Strategic Plan and the Retail CBDC FAQ. Project Atom, Dunbar and Acacia items are wholesale and were not listed (Acacia's consultation paper is already in the registry as AU_RBA_003). The mid-2022 to 2023 media releases on the DFCRC pilot launch, white paper and use cases (mr-22-23, mr-22-31, mr-23-06) are further minor status items left out because of the 12-item cap. Candidates: 12 (one, the Verian consultation report, is consultancy-authored and probably fails the authority rule).
coverage_notes.AW: AW (Centrale Bank van Aruba). Searched: cbaruba.org home page; the full Bank News listing crawled through getArticleList.do (270 items, about 2021 to Oct 2026), filtered for digital, CBDC, payments and fintech items; press releases, speeches & presentations, and papers pages (JavaScript-rendered, read with headless Chromium; the speeches and papers lists show no CBDC items); the Foro di Pago Nacional page and all five FPN summary reports (2023-2025); Operational Reports 2022, 2024 and 2025 with their condensed financial statements and press releases; the i-Pago instant-payments position paper (2022, no CBDC content); site-restricted web search. The Strategic Plan 2026-2030 'Ancra den Futuro' is hosted only as an Adobe InDesign viewer and could not be text-extracted, so its CBDC content, if any, is unchecked. The site was reachable. Judgement: MINOR GAPS. The CBA has no CBDC project and no formal policy statement on one. Beyond the registry's 2024 book chapter (AW_ARU_001), the only CBDC material is the Nov 2025 FPN conference presentation by a CBA economist on a retail digital florin (offline payments, permissioned DLT, three-tier KYC, pilots) and the Operational Report 2025 summary of it. Both are staff-level and corroborative, not a CBA decision. No status decision on a retail CBDC was found. The project's evidence base stays thin and staff-level. Candidates: 2.
coverage_notes.BS: BS (Central Bank of The Bahamas, Sand Dollar, live). Searched: centralbankbahamas.com - Digital Payments page, Digital Currency page, press releases (only the first page of 20 items loads; the ?page=N pagination is ignored both by plain HTTP and in headless Chromium, so older releases were found through web search and the cached URLs it returned), speeches list, Bank Supervision speeches & presentations, legal-framework and currency/payment legislation pages, annual reports 2019-2025 (2023, 2024 and 2025 searched in full text), Governor's quarterly briefings Q1-Q3 2026 (no Sand Dollar content); sanddollar.bs (official CBOB Sand Dollar site, FAQ); web search for CBOB Sand Dollar consultation, regulation and policy items. Covered 2019 to Oct 2026. The site was reachable, but many old /viewPDF/ links now return 404 because documents moved to cdn.centralbankbahamas.com. The 25 Sep 2020 public update could not be retrieved and is listed at low confidence. The 2024 statements that regulations would require all licensed institutions to give customers SandDollar access appear only in media interviews (Eyewitness News); I found no official CBOB document for them, so they are not listed. Judgement: MAJOR GAPS. The registry holds only the 2019 Project Sand Dollar paper (KEEP) and a 2025 news-listing page (DROP). It lacks the binding legal instruments: the 2021 Digital Currency Regulations with the tiered-wallet/KYC structure, the 2022 Holding and Transactional Limits Notice and the Central Bank Act 2020 legal-tender basis. It also lacks the 2021 consultation paper and policy paper (data privacy, tiers, limits), the Governor's 2022 lessons speech and the 2024 annual report on Wallet 2.0 data collection. For a live CBDC these are core design evidence. Candidates: 10.
coverage_notes.BT: BT (Royal Monetary Authority of Bhutan). Searched: rma.org.bt home page; publications pages (Macro-economic Data / annual reports 2016-2025; Payment & Settlement Systems quarterly reports 2019-Q3 2026); Digital Payment Ecosystem page; news/announcements, with all view_news items 1-192 (about 2023/24 to Oct 2026) fetched and full-text-searched for CBDC/digital ngultrum (no hits); Monetary Policy Statement 2026. Full-text checked: annual reports 2021-2025 (CBDC content in 2021, 2022 and 2024; none in 2023 or 2025), quarterly payment reports Q4 2021-Q3 2026 (no CBDC content). The site was reachable only in a browser: its TLS chain is incomplete, so curl fails, and PDFs were fetched by in-page fetch in headless Chromium. Press releases from before the current site, including any RMA release on the Sept 2021 Ripple pilot partnership, are no longer online. The Ripple/BusinessWire release is not an RMA channel and was not listed. Judgement: MAJOR GAPS relative to what the RMA has published. The registry holds only the 2021 roadmap (BORDERLINE). The 2024 annual report records a retail CBDC pilot with offline and programmability features and a phased path to nationwide rollout, a status and design statement missing from the registry. The 2021 annual report box documents the pilot launch, blockchain basis and objectives. Overall the RMA's official CBDC record is thin, with no dedicated CBDC publication, consultation or legislation found. Candidates: 3.
coverage_notes.CA: CA (Bank of Canada digital dollar; Payments Canada Jasper). Searched: bankofcanada.ca/digitaldollar hub and its 'What we heard 2020-23' page; the 2020 contingency-planning page; BoC press releases (May 2023 consultation launch, Nov 2023 what-we-heard); speeches (Lane Feb 2020, Feb 2021); annual reports 2023 and 2024 (Currency chapters); the digital-currencies-and-fintech research hub and staff author profiles (staff analytical notes 2020-6, 2020-9, 2022-14; discussion papers already in registry); web search for BoC CBDC items 2020-2026. Covered 2020 to Oct 2026; pre-2018 and Jasper material is already in the registry. The site was reachable with plain HTTP. Dates for the 2021 speech summary and both annual-report chapters are approximate (from the URL path or usual publication month), because page templates show only the current date. The Sept 2024 scale-down appears to have been announced on the digitaldollar topic page, which the registry holds as CA_BoC_ScaleDown_page_2024; I found no separate press release for it. Judgement: MAJOR GAPS. The registry lacks the founding Feb 2020 contingency-plan statement ('no plans to launch a CBDC') and the companion Lane speech. It also lacks the May 2023 release ('not needed ... decision rests with Parliament and the Government'), the Bank's own Nov 2023 engagement summary and releases with explicit privacy findings, and the 2024 annual report confirming that retail CBDC work was completed and wound down. The privacy and technology staff notes from the contingency programme (SAN 2020-6, 2020-9, 2022-14) are also missing. Payments Canada Jasper items after 2018 (e.g. Jasper-Ubin 2019) are wholesale and were not listed. Many further BoC staff working papers on CBDC exist (offline payments, adoption, monetary effects) and could be added if the authors want broader staff_research coverage; I listed only the three most design-relevant. Candidates: 12.
coverage_notes.CH: CH (SNB; Helvetia is wholesale; retail stance). Searched: snb.ch 'SNB explained: CBDC' page, Project Helvetia page and Q&A, the speeches listing (JavaScript-rendered; only the latest 20 items are reachable, with no archive or pagination), annual reports 2020-2024 (accountability reports, full-text searched for retail CBDC statements; I did not locate the 2025 report's PDF link). Older SNB speeches were found by checking titles and dates against the BIS central bankers' speeches mirror (used for discovery only) and confirming each on snb.ch through the ref_YYYYMMDD_initials URL pattern and its PDF asset; the 2018, 2019 (x2), 2021 and 2022 speeches were downloaded and full-text-checked. Also searched: admin.ch Federal Council release of 13 Dec 2019. Web search hit the session's search budget before I could check Federal Council answers to parliamentary motions and interpellations on an e-franc on parlament.ch; those (2020-2026) remain UNCHECKED and are the main open item. Two finds were left out: news reports of SNB staff remarks (Kraenzlin 2020, Moser 2023 interview), which are not official-channel documents, and the Maechler/Moser Apr 2021 and Schlegel Nov 2022 speeches, which mention CBDC only in passing. Judgement: MINOR GAPS for the retail stance. The registry already holds the 2019 Federal Council report, Jordan's 2024 retail-sceptical speech and the SNB CBDC explainer. Missing are the SNB's own formal posture statements in the 2021 and 2022 annual reports ('no additional benefits/utility in a retail CBDC'), the 2018 Maechler and 2019 Jordan speeches that first set out the retail stance, and the Federal Council release accompanying the 2019 report. No new wholesale-only Helvetia items were listed (the registry already has 2020-2025 Helvetia coverage). Candidates: 5.
coverage_notes.CL: CL Chile (Banco Central de Chile). Searched (2 Nov 2026, Spanish site; behind an Incapsula bot wall, so curl fails and all pages/PDFs were opened with headless Chromium): MDBC hub https://www.bcentral.cl/areas/hub-tecnologico-financiero/moneda-digital-de-banco-central (incl. hidden FAQ answers), its sub-pages Informes en MDBC and Prueba de Concepto MDBC, the older hub https://www.bcentral.cl/areas/observatorio-tecnologico/exploracion-de-monedas-digitales-de-banco-central (same FAQ, list of presentations 2021-2024; all presentations listed there are already in the registry), the contenido-general-mdbc fragment, the site search for "MDBC" (103 hits, mostly page fragments; pagination did not render), and the Informe de Sistemas de Pago page with full reports 2022, 2023, 2024 (no MDBC content), 2025 (Recuadro III.1) and 2026 (Recuadro III.3). Period covered: 2021 to Oct 2026. Not checked: Memoria anual (2023-2025), IEF boxes, Senate presentations after 2021, English site (English editions count as present anyway). Web-search budget ran out before the Memoria and IEF could be searched. Findings: the registry holds the two reports, their press releases and the 2021-2024 presentations, but it misses (a) the ISiP 2025 box that records the decision to move to an applied PoC phase and (b) the hub FAQ with explicit privacy/offline/status statements. Counterintuitive point to flag: the registered 'Prueba de Concepto MDBC' page (CL_..._Prueba-de-Concepto-MDBC_2025) describes a WHOLESALE PoC on Hyperledger Besu ('MDBC mayorista'); the ISiP 2026 box confirms it was wholesale-only, so that registry row should be flagged as wholesale for the retail matrix. Judgement: minor gaps (2 decision-relevant additions; ISiP 2022/2023 sections and the 2022 survey are low-weight).
coverage_notes.CN: CN China (People's Bank of China). Searched (2 Nov 2026): pbc.gov.cn (Chinese; reachable via headless Chromium) using the PBOC full-site search engine wzdig.pbc.gov.cn with exact phrases (数字人民币 + 可控匿名 / 个人信息保护 / 计付利息 / 行动方案 / 管理服务体系 / 运营管理中心 / 国际运营中心 / 计量框架 / 新一代数字人民币 / 研发试点 / 提案答复; leader names 易纲 / 范一飞 / 潘功胜 / 陆磊), the news list, the 2026 work-conference releases and the State Council financial-work reports (2022-2025, no e-CNY passages found); NPC draft-law consultation list www.npc.gov.cn/flcaw (JSON list endpoint). Period: 2019 to Oct 2026. Branch-office pages (shenzhen.pbc.gov.cn etc.) were seen in results but not listed: they are local outreach. English site not checked separately (English editions count as present). Findings: the registry holds only the 2021 white paper (KEEP), a misattributed BIS paper (DROP), a news-site copy of Lu Lei's 2025 article and the 2025 International Operation Center release. Missing are several governor-level privacy statements (Yi Gang 2021 BOFIT speech; Yi Gang HK FinTech Week 2022, which says the central bank does not process individual transaction data), the 2021 white-paper briefing transcript (no interest, tiered wallets, offline, programmability), the 2022 PBOC review article (privacy legal basis, offline hardware wallets, smart contracts), and the legal track (2020 PBOC Law draft for comment; NPC first-reading draft of June 2026 that 'clarifies the legal status of digital RMB'). For the e-CNY 2.0 shift, the Action Plan text is still not on pbc.gov.cn; official PBOC confirmations are Pan Gongsheng's 27 Oct 2025 speech (study repositioning e-CNY in monetary aggregates) and the 2 Mar 2026 release ('new-generation measurement framework'). Out of window: Pan Gongsheng's 2026 Financial Street Forum speech (pbc.gov.cn, published 2026-10-19, one day after the as-of date) states that the new framework went live at the start of 2026 and that e-CNY was repositioned 'from cash to deposit money'. It is the clearest official statement of the 2.0 decision but falls outside D1.4, and it is not listed. The NPC draft text returns 403 after its consultation closed, so it is listed with medium confidence. The search budget was exhausted before the PBOC English site and the annual reports could be checked. Judgement: major gaps (the retail privacy/data-access and legal-status evidence is largely missing; the 2.0 decision is only weakly sourced).
coverage_notes.CZ: CZ Czechia (Česká národní banka). Searched (2 Nov 2026; cnb.cz reachable by plain HTTP): CBDC landing page https://www.cnb.cz/cs/platebni-styk/digitalni-penize-centralnich-bank-cbdc/ and every item it links ('Napsali jsme o CBDC': 2020 čnBlog, Dědek 2022 slides, Nov 2022 press release, Kubíček 2025 comment, the 2022 publication); board-member articles/interviews section (Benda/Matějů 2021; Michl Dec 2025 and Jul 2026); čnBlog 'Euro a my: plány na digitální euro' (May 2025, staff, about the digital euro only). Period: 2020 to Oct 2026. Not checked: CNB annual reports and Financial Stability Reports for CBDC boxes, governor speeches in English, and Ministry of Finance (no Czech CBDC legislation is known; the CNB says current law does not permit issuance). Excluded: Kubíček 2025 'Digitální euro jako peněženka budoucnosti?' (about the ECB project, not a Czech CBDC) and the 2025 čnBlog on the digital euro. Findings: the registry holds only the 2022 working-group publication (BORDERLINE). The CNB has no CBDC project, but the official channel carries an explicit, current status statement (the Bank Board has taken no decision; legislation would have to change), a board member's 2022 design-posture slides (anonymity, wallet limits, intermediated wallets), and the Governor's July 2026 position that instant payments already are the 'digital koruna'. That is a counterintuitive posture signal: the CNB redefines 'digital koruna' as instant payments, not a CBDC. Judgement: minor gaps for a no-project jurisdiction; the landing-page status statement and Dědek 2022 are the decision-relevant additions.
coverage_notes.GH: GH Ghana (Bank of Ghana, eCedi). Searched (2 Nov 2026; bog.gov.gh reachable): WordPress site search for 'eCedi', 'CBDC', 'digital cedi', 'Giesecke', 'pilot' (all result pages); the speeches and news pages that matched; annual reports 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025 (full PDFs grepped). Period: 2021 to Oct 2026. Findings: the registry holds the 2021 Design Paper and the Oct 2024 eCedi Report. Missing are the Aug 2021 G+D pilot press release (status decision to pilot, retail, no-account access), the AR 2022 statement that online/offline field testing was completed, the Oct 2024 award release on design elements, the Dec 2023 Governor hackathon speech, and above all First Deputy Governor Mumuni's 19 Nov 2025 keynote (offline built in, traceability of every transaction, data-protection concern, separation of issuance and distribution modules). Not listed: Governor Asiama's 12 May 2025 IMF SSA CBDC seminar remarks (no eCedi-specific statement found). Counterintuitive: the BoG 2025 Annual Report (June 2026) contains no eCedi/CBDC mention at all, which may signal deprioritisation under the new governor. That is an absence, not a recorded decision. Not checked: MPC statements and the Payment Systems Act for CBDC amendments. Judgement: minor-to-moderate gaps; the Mumuni 2025 speech and the 2021 pilot press release are the important additions.
coverage_notes.HK: HK Hong Kong (HKMA, e-HKD / Project e-HKD+). Searched (2 Nov 2026): www.hkma.gov.hk via headless Chromium (direct curl to the site failed; the old e-HKD landing URL now returns 404) and the HKMA open-data press-release API (api.hkma.gov.hk/public/press-releases, all records 2019-06 to 2026-11, titles filtered for e-HKD/CBDC/digital money). The insight-articles API had no e-HKD titles; the speeches API was unavailable. Period: 2019 to Oct 2026. Findings: the registry holds the 2021 technical paper, the 2022 policy/design paper, the 2022 'Charting the next steps' annex and the 2025 Phase 2 report. It MISSES the e-HKD Pilot Programme Phase 1 Report (30 Oct 2023, 38 pp.), a major design/pilot document. It also misses the status-decision press releases: pilot commencement (May 2023), Phase 2 and the rename to Project e-HKD+ (Sep 2024), and the Oct 2025 release that records the decision to prioritise wholesale and defer retail (groundwork 'by the first half of 2026'). No 2026 e-HKD release was found in the API (only Project Ensemble/tokenisation, wholesale). So the announced H1-2026 retail groundwork or token standards were not found as a publication before the as-of date. Excluded: Project Sela (2022, BIS Innovation Hub-led; HKMA not lead), mBridge/Ensemble/LionRock (wholesale), and the 2021-10-04 and 2022-04-27 releases (they announce papers already registered). Not checked: LegCo Panel on Financial Affairs papers and HKMA speeches. Judgement: major gap (Phase 1 report) plus minor gaps (status releases).
coverage_notes.HU: HU Hungary (Magyar Nemzeti Bank). Searched (2 Nov 2026; mnb.hu via headless Chromium): English press-release lists 2021-2025 (first page of each year), the FinTech és Digitalizációs Jelentés series (2020-2025 editions; 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025 PDFs grepped), and the Student Safe press releases. The MNB site search returned no results. Period: 2020 to Oct 2026. Findings: the registry holds only the 2025 Student Safe white paper (EN; the Hungarian edition counts as present). Missing are the status records of the pilot: launch with real money (12 May 2023: 'first CBDC pilot … available to retail users', accounts kept directly by the MNB) and closure (2 Dec 2024: 'will be phased out'), plus the 2023 FinTech report box describing the pilot design. Counterintuitive: the November 2025 FinTech and Digitalisation Report (under the new MNB leadership) has no own-CBDC content; its only CBDC passages describe the US anti-CBDC stance. No MNB statement on a successor retail project was found. Not checked: annual reports, Payment Systems Reports, 2021 Matolcsy statements on a 'digital forint' (reported in media, not located on mnb.hu before the search budget ran out), and later-page press releases. Judgement: minor gaps (the 2024 discontinuation and the 2023 launch releases are the key additions).
coverage_notes.ID: ID Indonesia (Bank Indonesia, Project Garuda / Rupiah Digital). Searched (2 Nov 2026; bi.go.id via headless Chromium, intermittently refusing connections): Digital Rupiah project page in Indonesian and English (white paper, consultative paper, public consultation report, PoC report, FAQ with hidden answers), BI law page (UU BI) with UU 4/2023 P2SK, the consolidated Currency Law and UU 4/2026, and the payment-system blueprint page (BSPI 2025 and 2030 plus Q&A). The BI press-release listing and site search did not load (empty response/404), so press releases and Board speeches (e.g. the PTBI 2022 Project Garuda launch speech) could not be checked. BPK JDIH (peraturan.bpk.go.id) was blocked by Cloudflare. Period: 2019 to Oct 2026. Findings: the registry holds the 2022 white paper (EN), the 2023 wholesale consultative paper and the 2024 wholesale PoC report. Two of its three rows are wholesale-only, so retail evidence is thin. Missing: the statutory basis (UU 4/2023 P2SK makes 'Rupiah digital' a legal form of Rupiah, BI the sole manager), and BSPI 2030 (Aug 2024), which directs Rupiah Digital work in 2025-2030 to wholesale-market experimentation, a de facto deferral of retail. Also missing: the project FAQ (retail r-Rupiah Digital defined; complements cash; no issuance date) and the wholesale public consultation report. UU 4/2026 (amending P2SK) has no Rupiah-digital provisions. Judgement: moderate gaps (legislation and the BSPI 2030 direction are decision-relevant; press releases/speeches unchecked).
coverage_notes.IL: Searched the Bank of Israel English digital shekel hub (https://www.boi.org.il/en/economic-roles/payment-systems/future-payment-methods/digital-shekel-cbdc/), its publications list, press-release list and the linked FAQ (https://www.boi.org.il/en/questions-and-answers/digital-shekel/), plus the Hebrew hub (https://www.boi.org.il/roles/paymentsystems/future-means-payments/cbdc/), the Hebrew FAQ and the Hebrew 'public forums' pages (https://www.boi.org.il/publications/other-publications/public-forums/ and .../financial-forums/). Coverage runs back to the November 2018 team report; both sites were reachable via headless Chromium and all listed PDFs were downloaded and opened. The registry holds only the March 2024 logical architecture paper, an unidentified 2024 white paper (IL_BoI_2024) and the 2025 progress report, while the official publication list has eleven project documents plus an FAQ and speeches. Not listed: the Hebrew-only meeting summaries of the end-user forum (nine meetings, Jun 2023 to Mar 2026) and the financial-industry forum, which may contain design statements; BIS-led Project Sela and Icebreaker press releases (BIS Innovation Hub led, so not BoI-led consortia); press releases that only announce documents already listed (3 Mar 2025, 11 Mar 2024, 13 May 2026); and the Digital Shekel Challenge releases (2024), which describe a sandbox rather than design positions. If IL_BoI_2024 turns out to be the logical architecture paper, the registry has one fewer distinct document than it seems. Judgement: major gaps, especially the 2021 draft model, the 2022 response summary and the March 2025 preliminary design consultation, which is the key design-position document.
coverage_notes.IN: Searched rbi.org.in (legacy Scripts pages: press releases, speeches and media interactions, FAQ Id=169, Annual Report 2025-26 chapters) and website.rbi.org.in (currency-management speeches, interviews), plus Ministry of Finance channels (indiabudget.gov.in Budget 2022-23 speech and Finance Bill; pib.gov.in) and attempted egazette.gov.in and indiacode.nic.in for the enacted Finance Act 2022 (egazette failed TLS verification, indiacode timed out, so the Bill as introduced is cited instead). Coverage runs from July 2021 to October 2026. RBI legacy pages were reachable; rbidocs.rbi.org.in PDFs block scripted download, so the HTML versions were used. The registry holds only the October 2022 concept note and an unidentified 2025 explainer, which is probably an earlier edition of the FAQ. Missing are the status records (pilot launch, the 2022 budget announcement, the legal amendment) and the 2024 design announcements on programmability, offline use and non-bank wallets. Not listed for lack of an official transcript: Governor Das's May 2024 BIS Innovation Summit remarks on anonymity ('permanent deletion of transactions'), known only from news reports; the December 2022 post-policy remarks on anonymity of low-value transactions; and a Lok Sabha reply PDF on eparlib.sansad.in (connection reset). Earlier RBI Annual Reports (2022-23 to 2024-25) also have CBDC sections that were not opened individually. The October 2025 offline e₹ launch at Global Fintech Fest was found only in news, with no RBI press release located; the RBI HaRBInger 2025 release (23 Oct 2025) only names offline CBDC as a hackathon theme. Judgement: major gaps; the registry has no status-decision or legal-basis document and no record of the 2024 programmability and offline decisions.
coverage_notes.IS: Searched the Central Bank of Iceland Icelandic site (sedlabanki.is) using its site search for 'seðlabankarafeyri', 'rafkróna', 'rafkrónu' and 'CBDC'; the payments and financial-infrastructure page (https://sedlabanki.is/greidslumidlun/fjarmalainnvidir/), which links the bank's three CBDC publications; and the news items for each speech, plus web searches of cb.is (English). Coverage runs back to 2017; the site was reachable and all listed PDFs were opened. The registry holds only the 2018 'Rafkróna?' interim report (Sérrit 12), while the bank itself lists three CBDC publications (2018, 2023, 2025), so the March 2023 discussion paper (Sérrit 17), the main post-2018 design and consultation document, is missing. No English edition of Sérrit 17 or of the 2025 Vettvangur was found on cb.is, and no published summary of responses to Sérrit 17 was found. Not listed: Sérrit 13 (2018, retail payments and preparedness, published with Sérrit 12), which is about domestic payments rather than CBDC design, and a 2021 Kalkofninn staff blog post on fintech. The bank's current posture is that no decision has been taken (web page dated June 2026); 2024-2026 activity is otherwise about a domestic retail payment solution (not a CBDC). Judgement: major gaps relative to the bank's own short list, although the overall CBDC corpus for Iceland is small.
coverage_notes.JM: Searched the Bank of Jamaica CBDC hub (https://boj.org.jm/core-functions/currency/cbdc/) and its sub-pages 'BOJ Speaks', 'BOJ in the Press' (all external media, so excluded), FAQs and Ceremonial Minting; the annual publications page (annual reports 2016-2025); the BOJ speeches list (https://boj.org.jm/news/boj-speeches/), where the 2025-2026 Governor statements were checked and contain no JAM-DEX content; the BOJ site search for 'JAM-DEX'; and web searches for 2024-2026 BOJ releases and CBDC legislation. The site was reachable via headless Chromium. Coverage runs from 2020 to October 2026. The registry is already extensive (press releases 2020-2023, the 2022 Amendment Act, FAQs, wallet privacy policy, the 2021 and 2022 annual-report sections, the June 2026 Governor release). New candidates are mainly the 2023, 2024 and 2025 annual-report CBDC sections, which record roll-out status and the wallet-provider model, and the 2020 annual report. The only design-position op-ed found is a republication of a registry item. No 2024-2026 BOJ press release dedicated to JAM-DEX was found on boj.org.jm; JIS items (for example 'JAM-DEX Project Remains a Priority', Aug 2025) are government news reports of BOJ statements and were not listed. A Governor Langrin JCC talk (2026, 'Trust in Motion') is referenced on the CBDC hub only as a video or social post with no text found. Judgement: minor gaps (the registry covers 2020-2023 well; 2023-2025 status records are missing).
coverage_notes.JP: Searched the Bank of Japan English CBDC hub (https://www.boj.or.jp/en/paym/digital/index.htm), which lists the approach paper, all experiment and pilot releases, the Liaison and Coordination Committee material and eleven sets of committee opening remarks (2021-2026), and the Japanese hub (https://www.boj.or.jp/paym/digital/index.htm). Also searched the Ministry of Finance council pages for the Expert Panel on CBDC (https://www.mof.go.jp/about_mof/councils/meeting_of_cbdc/index.html) and the Relevant Ministries and BOJ Liaison Meeting on CBDC (https://www.mof.go.jp/about_mof/councils/meeting_of_cbdcre/index.html). Coverage runs from 2020 to October 2026; all sites were reachable and the listed PDFs and speeches were opened. The registry holds only four BoJ experiment reports (PoC1 2022, PoC2 2023, Pilot progress 2024 in JA and EN). It lacks the October 2020 approach paper and the whole government track (MoF expert panel December 2023; Liaison Meeting interim summaries April 2024 and May 2025; progress report June 2026), which carries the institutional design positions on personal data, holding limits and intermediaries. It also lacks the 2025 and 2026 pilot reports. Not listed (beyond the cap of 12): the April 2021 and March 2022 experiment-commencement releases (status records); the 2021 committee establishment release; other committee opening remarks (Mar 2021, Oct 2021, Nov 2022, Feb 2023 'Taking the Next Step', which records the pilot decision, and Jun 2026); the overview (gaiyou) versions of the MoF reports and meeting minutes and materials (2024-2026, including a 2026-10-08 meeting); the CBDC Forum page and its working-group materials; Payment and Settlement Systems Report briefs (privacy-enhancing technologies, Jan 2023), which are staff research; and Project Stella (wholesale DLT, so excluded). Judgement: major gaps.
coverage_notes.KE: Searched the Central Bank of Kenya site (https://www.centralbank.go.ke/): the discussion-papers page, the 10 Feb 2022 and 2 Jun 2023 CBDC news pages, the site search for 'digital currency' and 'Central Bank Digital Currency', and the National Payments Strategy 2022-2025 documents page (strategy, Governor's launch remarks, press release, presentation). Also ran web searches for 2024-2026 CBK statements on a CBDC. Coverage runs from 2022 to October 2026; the site was reachable and the listed PDFs were opened. The registry has only the February 2022 discussion paper, so the outcome document (May 2023 'Comments from the Public') and its 2 June 2023 press release, which records the status decision that a CBDC is not a priority in the short to medium term, are missing. Not listed: the Governor's NPS launch remarks (Feb 2022, generic mention of CBDC risks) and the 10 Feb 2022 web announcement of the discussion paper (a landing page for a registry item). No 2024-2026 CBK document revisiting the CBDC decision was found on the official site; later references (IMF reports, news) are not official CBK sources. Judgement: minor gaps in number (one or two documents), but the missing item is the decisive status and outcome record.
coverage_notes.KZ: Searched the National Bank of Kazakhstan digital tenge pages (https://nationalbank.kz/ru/page/digital-tenge and https://nationalbank.kz/ru/page/Digital-Tenge), which list ten project documents from May 2021 to December 2023; NBK information messages and press releases on the digital tenge (2023-2026, found by web search in Russian); the official legal portal Adilet (Law on Payments and Payment Systems, consolidated text); and the National Payment Corporation site (npck.kz) for the 2024 and 2025 reports. Searches were run in Russian. Kazakh and English editions exist for some items but were not separately checked, since English editions count as the same document. Coverage runs from May 2021 to October 2026; nationalbank.kz and adilet.zan.kz were reachable; file downloads and the NBK resolution (docx) were opened. The registry holds only the December 2021 pilot white paper and the December 2023 phase-one white paper. Missing are the May 2021 consultation and Q&A, the 2022 decision model, the December 2022 White Paper that recommended introduction (the key status-decision study), the September 2023 status report, the 2024-2026 legal basis (legal-tender law and the April 2026 NBK rules) and the 2024 and 2025 annual reports. The 2024 and 2025 reports are published by NPC, a wholly owned NBK subsidiary that operates the platform; authors should decide whether NPC counts as the competent body. Not listed: the July 2021 presentation inviting banks to the pilot; NBK information messages of 18 Sep and 15 Dec 2023 (announcements of listed reports); 27 May 2024 and 27 Jan 2025 messages (brief mentions of public-procurement and budget pilots); 2 Mar 2026 board message; and the Kazakh-language editions. Judgement: major gaps.
coverage_notes.MG: Searched banky-foibe.mg through its backend JSON endpoints (/admin/wp-json/bfm/actualite pages 1-51, i.e. all 303 news posts 2018-2026; /communiques; /media; detail-actualite for every e-Ariary-related post; page endpoints for annual reports and financial stability reports). Also checked annual reports 2020-2022 (the latest published), the 2025-2026 monetary policy reports and bulletins (no e-Ariary mentions), and the e-Ariary one-pager and 2024 brochure. Period covered: 2020-Oct 2026. The site serves an incomplete chain; the SSL.com intermediate was added to a local bundle, with verification on. Registry rows (RFI 2021, 'MG_BFM_2023', 'MG_BFM_OP_2023') have no titles or URLs, so matches are uncertain. The 2020 one-pager may be MG_BFM_OP_2023 and the 2022 Annual Report (published Oct 2023) may be MG_BFM_2023. The most design-relevant new item is the March 2024 brochure 'eAriary - Une nouvelle forme de l'Ariary au service de tous' (posted Apr 2025). It covers intermediated distribution, cash-like rules, usability without a bank account, phone or internet, and protection of personal and transaction data. The 23 May 2025 public launch of the 10-month e-Ariary experimentation phase is reported by the press (L'Express, Newsmada) but no BFM communiqué, report or speech on it was found on the official site. That status decision is therefore undocumented on official channels as far as this search can tell. The Malagasy-language brochure is the same document. Judgement: minor-to-moderate gaps. The brochure and annual-report boxes add design and status content, but there is no official record of the 2025 pilot launch.
coverage_notes.MO: Searched amcm.gov.mo: the news API (/api/v1.0/cms/news, all 452 press releases 2019-Oct 2026, full text searched for 數字澳門元/e-MOP/央行數字貨幣/mBridge), the e-MOP special pages (/news-notice/Special_Coverage/emop/: introduction, white paper, white paper slides, prototype slides, FAQ '數字澳門元知識解答'), and AMCM annual reports 2023-2025. Also Boletim Oficial for Lei n.º 10/2023 (read through WebFetch because the direct download failed with proxy 502). Legislative Assembly PDFs (al.gov.mo attachments from 2024-2026 that search engines return for 數字澳門元) redirect automated clients to the homepage and could not be opened; they may contain policy-address debate material or a special e-MOP law and should be checked manually. The registry holds only the Dec 2024 white paper. Missing: the legal basis (Law 10/2023: digital currency is legal tender, special law to follow), the Sep 2024 and Dec 2024 press releases (legal status, phasing, tiered and hardware wallets, smart contracts, retail first), the e-MOP FAQ (controllable anonymity with anonymous and real-name account tiers, compliance with the personal data law, offline and no-account use being explored), the prototype slides, and 2025-2026 status records (core system done Q4 2025, whitelist sandbox, next scenarios e-gov, transport and campus). The mBridge launch (Jun 2026) is wholesale and listed separately. Judgement: major gaps; the registry covers one document while the official channel has a legal basis, a privacy FAQ and a status trail through 2026.
coverage_notes.MU: Searched bom.mu: the CBDC FAQ page (https://www.bom.mu/cdbc-FAQs), the CBDC consultation paper and public notices, media releases, all 351 speech pages listed under /media/speeches (140 governor and deputy-governor speeches and MPC statements were downloaded and text-searched), annual reports for the years ended June 2021-2025, and the consolidated Bank of Mauritius Act (Aug 2023). Also checked the Finance (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2020 on mra.mu, which amended the BoM Act to define 'digital currency'. Period covered: 2020-Oct 2026. bom.mu serves an incomplete certificate chain. Pages were fetched with the missing Sectigo intermediate added to a local CA bundle; TLS verification stayed on. The registry holds only the June 2023 consultation paper. It misses the design decisions announced in the April 2023 CCBT keynote (interest-free, two-tier distribution), the CBDC FAQ (privacy, two-tier model, objectives), the Jan 2024 notice that the pilot had started, the statutory basis (BoM Act ss. 35-37: sole issuer, legal tender, power to make rules and to open accounts), and annual-report records showing the pilot ran Nov 2023-Apr 2024 on a permissioned blockchain. It also misses the July 2025 speech by the new governor saying the Bank is 'still studying' a retail CBDC that must not compete with IPS and flagging privacy concerns. Judgement: major gaps; the registry is a single document for a project with a pilot, a legal basis and a later change of posture.
coverage_notes.NA: Searched bon.com.na: the Strategy, Projects and Transformation department page (it links the Oct 2022 CBDC consultation paper and the thought-leadership event), media releases and speeches found via site search, the annual reports 2021-2025 (Publications/Annual-Reports), and older position papers on virtual currencies (2017, 2018; pre-2018 or non-CBDC, not listed). The site was reachable. No BoN discussion paper, roadmap or FAQ on a CBDC beyond the 2022 consultation paper was found. Per the press, the IMF TA report 'Retail CBDC Exploration and Roadmap' (Feb 2025) is an IMF publication and was excluded. The Dec 2025 governor podcast remarks (5-10 year horizon) were reported only in the press and no official transcript was found. The most important new item is the 2025 Annual Report (published ~Apr 2026). It records that the exploration 'was refocused on institutional use cases', away from retail and toward wholesale/CMA cross-border work. This is a status-relevant shift. Judgement: minor gaps in volume but one material status gap (the 2025 retail-to-wholesale refocus). Other items are speeches and press releases from 2022-2024 with objective and posture statements.
coverage_notes.NG: Searched the CBN website through its JSON listing endpoints (cbn.gov.ng/api/GetAllNews, GetAllPressReleases, GetAllCirculars, GetAllSpeeches, GetAllPublications, GetAllReports, GetAllNotices; fetched live on 2 Nov 2026), the CBN eNaira page (https://www.cbn.gov.ng/Currency/eNaira.html), CBN annual and annual economic reports 2021, 2022 and 2025, and the 2022/23 Monetary, Credit, Foreign Trade and Exchange Policy Guidelines. Period covered: 2021-2026. The dedicated eNaira site (https://enaira.gov.ng) could not be reached from this sandbox (TLS cipher mismatch). The Design Paper on that site was read through WebFetch. The eNaira FAQ is blocked by robots.txt for automated fetching and was not reviewed. The registry (Regulatory Guidelines 2021 and the 2023 diaspora framework) misses the most important design source, the eNaira Design Paper of Oct 2021 (Hyperledger Fabric, tiered KYC wallets with caps, no interest, data use, offline and smart contracts on the roadmap). It also misses the launch and technical-partner press releases, the 2022/23 policy guidelines (phased, tiered-KYC implementation), the 2021 and 2022 annual economic reports, and two staff publications. No speeches by CBN officials on eNaira appear in the CBN speech list. No CBN document after Oct 2023 mentions eNaira except, according to press reports, the 2024-2025 policy guidelines; that official PDF was not located. The 2025 CBN Annual Report (Jul 2026) has zero eNaira mentions, which is a signal of de-emphasis but not a recorded status decision. Judgement: major gaps, chiefly the missing Design Paper. Someone should also manually check the enaira.gov.ng FAQ and any eNaira-site notices.
coverage_notes.NO: Searched Norges Bank's English and Norwegian CBDC topic pages (https://www.norges-bank.no/en/topics/payment-system/central-bank-digital-currency/ incl. /assessment-of-cbdc/, /testing-of-cbdc/ and the FAQ; Norwegian /tema/betalingssystemet/digitale-sentralbankpenger/), news items 2020-2026, the Norges Bank Papers / Norges Bank Memo and Staff Memo listings, Financial Infrastructure reports 2020-2026 (/aktuelt/publikasjoner/Finansiell-infrastruktur---rapport/), and speeches (2020 and 2021 payments-conference speeches, 2023 BIS remarks). Period covered: 2018-Oct 2026. Site fully reachable (JS rendering via headless Chromium). The registry already holds the memo series 2018-2021, the Phase 4 final report, FI 2024 and the two 2026 Phase 5 papers, but it misses the decision-bearing items of Dec 2025-Mar 2026: the 10 Dec 2025 press release announcing that a CBDC is 'currently not warranted', the 24 Mar 2026 release, the assessment-of-CBDC topic page, and the FAQ, which states that the central bank should not have access to individuals' payment and holdings data. It also misses Norges Bank Papers 2/2026 (digital euro, with a section on the need for a Norwegian retail CBDC), Papers 3/2023 (Phase 4 testing), the Dec 2023 Phase 5 release, the FI 2023/2025/2026 CBDC sections and two speeches. Staff Memo 1/2026 is wholesale-only and is listed separately. Not listed (low marginal value): FI 2020-2022 CBDC sections, the 2023 'singleness of money' BIS remarks (mentions programmability), Strategy 28 (Dec 2025). Judgement: minor gaps for documents, major gap for the status decision: the Dec 2025 not-warranted decision and the privacy FAQ are not in the registry as standalone sources.
coverage_notes.NP: Searched nrb.org.np: the site search for 'CBDC' and 'central bank digital currency', the monetary policy category (English full texts 2021/22-2025/26 plus the 2025/26 annual review and the mid-term reviews), Payment Systems Oversight Reports 2022/23-2024/25, the Strategic Plan 2022-2026, and the governor-speech RSS feed (anniversary addresses 2024-2026 in Nepali, Preeti-encoded PDFs read by keyword). Also checked the House of Representatives bill register (https://hr.parliament.gov.np/np/bills, all three pages). The NRB site intermittently resets connections and serves a wrong intermediate certificate. Fetches succeeded after adding the Sectigo DV R36 intermediate to a local bundle, with verification on. The registry holds only the Aug 2022 concept/consultation report. Key missing item: the Nepal Rastra Bank (Third Amendment) Bill 2083, registered 25 May 2026 by the Ministry of Finance and now in the Finance Committee. It redefines currency to include NRB-issued digital currency and empowers issuance. Also missing: the monetary-policy commitments from feasibility study (2021) to further action (2023) to wholesale-first design (2024), the oversight report recording a pilot target of 2026 and a wholesale prototype, and anniversary speeches on the CBDC Division, prototypes and a 2026 SICPA sandbox agreement. Note: NRB's operational track is wholesale-first; retail design content after 2022 is thin. A Nepali-language explainer (Aug 2023, crypto vs CBDC) has no design statement and was not listed. Judgement: major gaps for status and legislation; minor for design.
coverage_notes.NZ: Searched (Nov 2, 2026) via headless browser and site-restricted web search: RBNZ digital cash hub https://www.rbnz.govt.nz/money-and-cash/future-of-money/digital-cash and sub-pages (FAQ, 'What you told us', 'Why we're looking into digital cash'), the Future of money section, the payments modernisation pages and 2026 issues paper (https://consultations.rbnz.govt.nz/rbnz/payments-modernisation-issues-paper), the Citizen Space consultation hub https://consultations.rbnz.govt.nz/money-and-cash/digital-cash-in-new-zealand/ (2024 consultation paper, four consultation notes, Dec 2024 response, storyboard), RBNZ news listing (2021-2026), annual report 2026 page, and rbnz.govt.nz search results for 2021-2022 Future of Money material. Back to 2021. HTML pages and the consultations subdomain were reachable; PDFs under rbnz.govt.nz/-/media return HTTP 403 to automated clients (one read via WebFetch; info release #6279 could not be opened). Key finding: the digital cash page now states RBNZ has PAUSED work on Digital Cash to focus on payments modernisation (reported 13 Oct 2026, before the 18 Oct as-of date) - a status decision not in the registry; no dedicated media release was found in the news listing, so the page itself (and possibly info release #6279) is the official record. Judgement: MAJOR GAPS - the registry holds only the 2021 issues paper and the 2024 insights dossier, missing the full April 2024 consultation package (paper + 4 design notes, incl. the privacy note), the Dec 2024 response, the 2022 summary of responses and the 2026 pause.
coverage_notes.PE: Searched (Nov 2, 2026): BCRP CBDC project page https://www.bcrp.gob.pe/sistema-de-pagos/proyecto-cbdc.html, the pilots page https://www.bcrp.gob.pe/sistema-de-pagos/proyecto-cbdc/pilotos-de-innovacion-de-dinero-digital.html and its FAQ, the notas informativas listing https://www.bcrp.gob.pe/transparencia/actividades-oficiales/notas-informativas.html (back to 2019), the Reporte del Sistema Nacional de Pagos y Fintech listing (2024-2026, HTML editions), the BCRP research portal (investigacion.bcrp.gob.pe), Spanish-language site-restricted web search, and El Peruano (official gazette) for Circular 0011-2024-BCRP. Site reachability: HTML pages render in a headless browser, but every PDF under bcrp.gob.pe/docs is blocked by Incapsula bot protection (curl, WebFetch and browser all get a challenge page), so press notes, the Annex, RGG 0009-2024 and the Moneda article are listed from their official titles/links with medium/low confidence; the Circular was read on El Peruano and the payments reports via their HTML editions. The press-reported pilot extension to March 2027 (June 2026) could not be traced to an official BCRP document. Registry holds only the 2023 presentation and one 2024 nota informativa. Judgement: MAJOR GAPS - the pilot's legal basis (Circular 0011-2024), the FAQ with explicit anonymisation/data-access statements, the pilot status notes and the payments-report sections are missing.
coverage_notes.PW: Searched (Nov 2, 2026): Palau government portal https://www.palaugov.pw/ (site search for 'stablecoin', the program page https://www.palaugov.pw/stablecoin/, news listing https://www.palaugov.pw/news/), plus web search for Ministry of Finance / Olbiil Era Kelulau material on the Palau Stablecoin and the National Digital Payment System bill (2021-2026). The palaugov.pw site returns 403 to the headless browser but is readable via WebFetch; all four PDFs listed were opened through WebFetch. Ripple/Business Wire press releases (Nov 2021 MOU, Jul 2023 launch) exist but are not on an official Palau channel, so they are excluded; no MOF press releases on the stablecoin were found on palaugov.pw. Note: the project is a government (MOF)-issued USD-backed token on the XRP Ledger, not a central-bank currency (Palau uses the USD), so subject eligibility depends on the dataset's PW framing. Judgement: MAJOR GAPS relative to the single registry row (Phase 1 report): the Phase 2a report (status/next phase), the 2023 FAQs (explicit privacy/KYC statements) and the draft Digital Payment System Bill (data protection, issuance) are missing; the audit report is a borderline-authority status source.
coverage_notes.RU: Searched (Nov 2, 2026): Bank of Russia digital ruble section https://www.cbr.ru/PSystem/dr/ (project history, FAQ, documents/rules pages), cbr.ru site search (queries on 'цифрового рубля', concept, 820-П, mass rollout, offline; several result pages), individual press items (2020-2026), board decisions (https://www.cbr.ru/rbr/), the NPS main directions 2025-2027, the commercial smart-contract platform concept; legislation via kremlin.ru document bank and acts news (laws 339-FZ, 340-FZ, 610-FZ, 105-FZ, 248-FZ, 303-FZ). Back to 2020. cbr.ru (no www) shows a browser-check page to headless browsers, but www.cbr.ru served HTML and PDFs to plain HTTP; kremlin.ru fully reachable; sozd.duma.gov.ru unreachable. Not listed (lower priority, available if wanted): 610-FZ (tax control incl. suspension of digital ruble accounts, Dec 2023), 303-FZ (budget process, Jul 2025), BoR board decision of 29.09.2026 on deadlines for banks under resolution, press 'Банк России предложил новые даты массового внедрения' (25.06.2025), Nov 2020 consultation-discussion press, annual-report/ONRFR sections, platform standards and account agreements, the English-site editions. Judgement: MAJOR GAPS - the registry (2020 consultation paper, 2021 concept, 2025 status report) lacks all federal laws, the platform regulation, the status-decision press releases (pilot start 2023, rollout law 2025, launch 1 Sept 2026) and the 2026 smart-contract concept.
coverage_notes.RW: Searched (Nov 2, 2026): National Bank of Rwanda CBDC page https://www.bnr.rw/financialinnovation (all six listed documents expanded and their PDF URLs captured), BNR homepage navigation, Publications/Monetary Policy pages, MPFSS March 2024 and March 2025 (no CBDC mentions), Monetary Policy Reports, the Annual Financial Stability Report, and the National Financial Inclusion Roadmap 2025-2030; site-restricted web search for press releases/speeches (2021-2026). Site reachable (HTML via headless browser, PDFs via HTTP). No BNR press-release section with CBDC items was found; the Feb 2026 'moves to pilot phase' news is based on the PoC report already in the registry (which records the next step: a 12-month pilot, no issuance decision). MPFSS 2026 editions could not be located. Judgement: MINOR-TO-MODERATE GAPS - the 2024 feasibility research paper (the main design document: token-based, offline, two-tier, privacy) and the 2025 FAQ (status) are missing from the registry and are the important additions; the rest are supporting.
coverage_notes.SE: Searched (Nov 2, 2026): Riksbank e-krona hub https://www.riksbank.se/en-gb/payments--cash/e-krona/ and its 'E-krona reports' and 'Published about e-krona' listings (2017-2026), individual news/press items, the Payments Report series (Payments in Sweden 2019-2020, Payments Report 2021-2026 section links), consultation responses (domestic), the Oct 2026 official communication to the Riksdag Finance Committee, and the SOU 2023:16 link on regeringen.se. Swedish-language pages exist for each item (e.g. 'Skrivelse: information om utveckling som aktualiserar frågan om digital krona'); English editions used. Site fully reachable. coverage_notes.SG: Searched (Nov 2, 2026): MAS Project Orchid page https://www.mas.gov.sg/schemes-and-initiatives/project-orchid, MAS media releases, speeches and parliamentary replies (2021-2026) via site-restricted web search and direct page loads, the Nov 2021 retail CBDC paper, the PBM whitepaper page and the Orchid Blueprint. Plain HTTP to mas.gov.sg returns a 'Maintenance' page, but pages render in a headless browser and the 2021 PDF was read via WebFetch. Wholesale-only items found and excluded from the list: Project Ubin, Orchid wholesale CBDC pilots (Nov 2023 'live' wholesale CBDC), SGD Testnet and tokenisation plans (Nov 2024), BLOOM (2025); 2025 parliamentary replies on stablecoins/GENIUS Act did not mention retail CBDC in the matched text. No document after Nov 2023 restating the retail CBDC stance was found (the Orchid page already in the registry carries the current 'no urgent need' line). Judgement: MAJOR GAPS - the registry (Orchid Phase 1 report, Orchid page) lacks the core stance documents: the Nov 2021 retail CBDC paper, the Mar 2022 parliamentary reply ('not compelling'), the 2021-2022 MD speeches, and the Nov 2023 Orchid Blueprint.
coverage_notes.SZ: Searched the Central Bank of Eswatini site (reachable, WordPress): the CBDC project page https://www.centralbank.org.sz/cbdc/ (created 2021-10-06, last modified 2025-11-28), the Fintech page https://www.centralbank.org.sz/financial-technology-fintech/, the FAQ https://www.centralbank.org.sz/faq/, the site's WordPress search and media-library API (queries CBDC, digital lilangeni, digital currency, pilot, offline, annual report), the Annual Integrated Reports 2020 to 2024/25, the Governor's annual-report presentation speeches (Oct 2023, Aug 2024), the Dec 2023 Financial Stability Report and the Annual Economic Reviews 2021/22 to 2025/26, back to 2019. Web search was used only to discover titles. The registry holds only the 2024 Digital Lilangeni Design Paper, so coverage has major gaps: it lacks the status decision (Governor's speech of 28 Aug 2024 says a full CBDC launch "will not be pursued at this time"; the CBDC page says the CBE "has decided not to proceed with issuing a CBDC at the moment"), the earlier May 2023 Initial Design Paper (final pre-pilot edition, plus the stakeholder-comment draft, which states partial pseudo-anonymity), the 2023/24 Annual Integrated Report section on the PoC/pilot and offline testing, the Oct 2022 press release, the Nov 2022 CBDC Briefing and the 2020 Diagnostic Study (Cenfri-authored, CBE-published). No separate pilot report or legislation was found. The Project Sunbird (CMA cross-border) material is wholesale and is not listed.
coverage_notes.TH: Searched the Bank of Thailand site (reachable; JavaScript-rendered, read with headless Chromium) in English and Thai: the CBDC hub https://www.bot.or.th/en/financial-innovation/digital-finance/central-bank-digital-currency-tokenization-emerging-payment-technologies.html and CBDC page .../central-bank-digital-currency.html (timeline, retail and wholesale project lists, report links, FAQ), the press releases linked there (2021-04-02, 2021-08-19, 2022-08-05, 2022-10-30 Thai, 2024-04-11, 2024-10-29), the annual reports 2022 to 2025 (EN), the Feb 2022 Financial Landscape consultation paper, and web searches in Thai and English for BOT news and speeches back to 2020. The annual reports 2022 to 2024 repeat the status position; the 2025 annual report has no retail CBDC content. No governor speech on bot.or.th with a retail-CBDC design statement was found (a 2022 governor quote reported by Central Banking could not be traced to an official page). Wholesale work (Inthanon 1-2, Inthanon-LionRock, mBridge, the 2020-21 corporate/supply-chain CBDC with SCG, which BOT classifies as wholesale, Project San and Programmable Payment sandbox) is excluded. The undated CBDC hub page's status line could not be dated before the as-of date.
coverage_notes.TR: Searched the CBRT site (reachable; read with headless Chromium): English press-release lists 2021 to 2026 (https://www.tcmb.gov.tr/wps/wcm/connect/EN/TCMB+EN/Main+Menu/Announcements/Press+Releases/<year>), Turkish press-release lists (…/TR/TCMB+TR/Main+Menu/Duyurular/Basin/<year>), the "Remarks by the Governor" lists 2022 to 2026 (one relevant Governor presentation found, Sept 2024), the CBRT Blog (EN/TR), the annual reports 2021 to 2025 (www3.tcmb.gov.tr/yillikrapor), and web searches in Turkish and English back to 2020. The registry holds the Phase 1 Evaluation Report (Dec 2023) and the Phase 2 Progress Report (Nov 2025), which are the substantive design documents, so coverage has minor gaps: it lacks the 2021 and 2022 press releases (status "no final decision", DLT, digital identification), the Sept 2025 call document and press release and the Aug 2026 results release (programmable payments, self-sovereign identity), and the Jan 2025 CBRT staff blog on design choices (two-tier, no bank account required, offline, optional use; staff_research). The cover press releases for the two registry reports are listed as "possibly". No DTL legislation was found. Government documents (Presidential Annual Programmes, 12th Development Plan), which mention DTL targets, were not checked in depth.
coverage_notes.TW: Searched the CBC site www.cbc.gov.tw (reachable; read with headless Chromium and direct PDF download): all press releases (lp-302) from Aug 2019 to Oct 2026 (about 100 list pages; the only CBDC release is 2026-04-15), all post-MPC press-conference reference materials and Q&A pages (lp-357) from 2020 to Sept 2026 (CBDC notes 2020-06, 2020-12, 2021-06, 2024-06, 2025-06), the reports to the Legislative Yuan (lp-2169) 2019 to 2026 (special reports 2021-11-01 and 2024-07-08; CBDC sections in the business reports 2021-03 to 2026-03), the video page, a 2022 governor speech, and the FSR/annual-report CBDC boxes found by web search. The registry holds only the April 2026 communication summary report, so coverage has major gaps: it lacks the July 2024 special report to the Legislative Yuan, which sets the planned design (named vs anonymous tiered wallets with caps, KYC, privacy, non-interest at launch, two-tier), the Nov 2021 readiness report (privacy, offline, programmability), the June 2024 survey note, the June 2022 governor speech on the trial (centralised architecture, DLT limits), and the Oct 2025 and Mar 2026 business reports recording the status position ("no urgency to issue a retail CBDC"; the prototype was repurposed as a payment platform for government digital vouchers). The Oct 2026 business report (2026-10-28) is after the as-of date and is excluded. All sources are in Chinese; no English editions were checked.
coverage_notes.UA: Searched the NBU site (reachable; read with headless Chromium): the e-hryvnia page in Ukrainian and English (https://bank.gov.ua/ua/payments/e-hryvnia, https://bank.gov.ua/en/payments/e-hryvnia) and all documents linked there (2019 pilot report, CBDCinUA2020 report, 2021 survey, 2023 draft vision, strategies), the FAQ (https://bank.gov.ua/en/faq#e_hryvnia), and NBU news found by web search in Ukrainian and English (2021-12-15, 2022-11-28), back to 2019. The site's own search did not return news results. The Verkhovna Rada law portal (zakon.rada.gov.ua) refused connections, so the Law on Payment Services could not be opened. NBU annual reports were not checked. The registry holds only the 2019 pilot analytical note and the 2025 web page, so coverage has major gaps: it lacks the 2023 Draft Vision of introducing the e-hryvnia, the key design and privacy document (NBU sees flows across all wallets; identified wallets; anonymous wallets with limits under consideration), the Nov 2022 concept press release, the 2021 expert-survey results (anonymity, offline), the FAQ's privacy and offline statements, and the 2021 Law on Payment Services, which gives the e-hryvnia its legal basis. Statements reported in media (Deputy Governor Shaban, Nov 2024 and Mar 2025, on a planned DLT-based pilot and no issuance decision) could not be traced to an official NBU page and are not listed. No pilot launch or final decision after 2023 was found on official channels.
coverage_notes.UK: Searched the Bank of England digital pound hub https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/the-digital-pound, its news page (…/the-digital-pound/digital-pound-news), the Lab pages, the explainers, the BoE CBDC-tagged news, publications and speeches listings (2016 to Oct 2026), the 2026 speeches by Bank officials (none mention the digital pound), and GOV.UK via its official search/content API (HMT news stories, consultation pages, the National Payments Vision and its delivery committee updates). The site was reachable but bankofengland.co.uk rate-limits (some pages returned 403 and were retried slowly or read on GOV.UK). Coverage runs from 2020 to the as-of date. The registry's 20 rows cover the main BoE/HMT papers well, so coverage has minor gaps. Missing are the joint status statements (Apr 2021 Taskforce, Nov 2021 next steps), the GOV.UK news stories of Feb 2023 and Jan 2024, which carry explicit privacy and programmability commitments ("would not be anonymous", "would not program", "would not have access to any personal data", privacy guaranteed in primary legislation), Cunliffe's Feb 2023 speech, the 2021 "New forms of digital money" discussion paper and its 2022 response, HMT's National Payments Vision (Nov 2024, "no decision"), the Governor's letter of 29 Jan 2026 to the Treasury Committee, and the Digital Pound Lab Phase 2 update (last updated 6 Oct 2026; one-time aliases, programmability). Also relevant but not listed because of the 12-item cap: the Cunliffe speeches of May 2021 and Oct 2023, the Payments Vision Delivery Committee update of 15 Jul 2025, and the Taskforce terms of reference (GOV.UK, 2024). Parliament (Lords Economic Affairs Committee 2022 report and government response; Treasury Committee material) could not be opened (publications.parliament.uk returned 403) and was not checked. The web-search budget ran out during this project, so 2024 to 2026 speeches by Breeden, Mills and others were checked only where the listings surfaced them; a reported Oct 2026 Breeden remark ("no reason to rush") could not be traced to an official page.
coverage_notes.UY: Searched the BCU site (https://www.bcu.gub.uy; reachable in Chromium, but its SharePoint site search returns an error and its certificate chain fails in curl): every news item in the current news system (Detalle-Noticia.aspx?noticia=1 to 564, covering about mid-2021 to Oct 2026) scanned for e-Peso, billete digital, CBDC, moneda digital and digital; the payment-system pages (Sistema de Pagos, oversight library "Libros", Reportes) and the studies/working-papers page. Only three relevant items were found: two 2021-22 news items with the BCU President's statements and a 2022 staff paper on the e-Peso pilot. Pre-2021 press releases (the 2017-18 pilot announcements), annual reports (Memoria Anual) and strategic plans could not be located at guessed URLs, and the web-search budget was exhausted before this project, so discovery for 2017-2020 relied only on site navigation. The registry's two items (2017 pilot document, Seven Lessons paper) cover the pilot. No BCU document after 2022 records a new e-Peso phase, design or decision (the "new steps next year" announced in Oct 2022 did not appear in any news item through Oct 2026). Coverage judgement: minor gaps for 2021 to 2026 (statement-level items only); possibly gaps for 2017 to 2020 (pilot-era press releases and annual reports), which were not checked.
coverage_notes.ZA: Searched the SARB site (https://www.resbank.co.za; reachable in headless Chromium, while direct downloads are bot-blocked, so PDFs were fetched in the browser): the Fintech page (…/what-we-do/fintech), the position-paper landing page for the Nov 2025 retail CBDC Position Paper and its companion Background Note, the Papers/position-papers list, the media-release listings by year 2021 to 2025 (the listing appears paginated or partial, about 30 items per year), and the 2026 Governor speech on payments (no CBDC content). The site's own search returns "page not found", and the web-search budget was exhausted before this project, so the 2021 announcement of the retail (general-purpose) CBDC feasibility study, any 2022-24 progress statements, and Governor or Deputy Governor speeches on retail CBDC could not be located. The registry holds Khokha 1 and 2 (wholesale), the Khokha 2 media release and the Nov 2025 Position Paper (the status decision). New are the companion Background Note (feasibility-study results: two-tier deployment models, privacy, offline, programmability) and the publication notice that states the decision. Project Dunbar (2021) is listed for reference only, as wholesale. Coverage judgement: minor gaps for the decision record, which is captured; possible further gaps for 2021-24 statement-level items (feasibility-study launch release, speeches, annual-report sections), which were not checked.
